topStories.headline: Another Planet Sues Castro Theatre Contractor Over 'Badly Botched' Renovation
topStories.dek: Another Planet Entertainment filed suit against contractor Alarcon Bohm this week, alleging defective work including roof leaks that damaged the historic theater's newly restored ceiling.
topStories.body:
Another Planet Entertainment (APE), the Berkeley-based concert promoter that operates San Francisco's iconic Castro Theatre, filed a civil lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court on August 3 against general contractor Alarcon Bohm Corporation and its principal Kevin Bohm, alleging defective construction work, excessive billing, and trademark infringement in connection with the $41 million renovation of the 104-year-old venue.

According to the complaint, the contractor allegedly performed defective and incomplete work, failed to pay subcontractors, and submitted bills exceeding the project's guaranteed maximum price by millions of dollars. Most alarmingly, the lawsuit alleges that extensive roof leaks damaged the historic ceiling — portions of which collapsed onto the balcony — shortly after the theatre reopened in February 2026. The suit also cites faulty drainage and improperly installed HVAC equipment. Repair and delay costs tied to the contractor's work were estimated at more than $5 million.

A spokesperson for Another Planet confirmed that the Castro Theatre remains open and safe for guests and performers while the litigation proceeds. A separate arbitration proceeding over construction cost disputes was already underway; the contractor claims it is still owed $4.7 million that APE says it does not owe.

The Castro Theatre reopened in February 2026 after a two-year closure for the $41 million renovation, which updated lighting and sound systems, restored historic murals and the original Pfleuger-designed ceiling, and reconfigured the floor for both seated and standing-room events. The theatre had been managed by APE since 2022 under a long-term lease with the Nasser family, who have owned the building since it opened in 1922.

topStories.headline: BART Schedule Overhaul Takes Effect Monday — What Glen Park Riders Need to Know
topStories.dek: A systemwide BART schedule change launching August 10 promises longer trains, more even headways, and redesigned operations at Daly City — with some departure times shifting by several minutes.
topStories.body:
Beginning Monday, August 10, BART will implement its most significant schedule reorganization in years, affecting riders throughout San Francisco including those using the Glen Park station. The agency says the changes are designed to reduce crowding, cut platform wait times, and improve transfer connections across the system.

Key changes include longer peak-hour trains on the Red, Yellow, Blue, and Green lines, which BART began phasing in on July 20. Under the new schedule, trains will be more evenly spaced: riders heading toward Bay Fair, for example, will wait no more than 12 minutes between trains, down from a previous gap of up to 17 minutes. Yellow and Red line trains will also be spaced 10 minutes apart instead of the current uneven 5-and-15 minute pattern.

The most significant physical change involves Daly City station, which will be reconfigured as a center-platform station. All San Francisco-bound trains will depart from a single platform, simplifying boarding. Blue and Green Line passengers traveling beyond Daly City to SFO Airport or Millbrae should transfer at Balboa Park instead of Daly City.

Because some departure times are shifting by a few minutes, BART is urging all riders — including regular Glen Park commuters — to recheck their trips using the BART Trip Planner with a trip date of August 10 or later. Updated PDF schedules are already posted at bart.gov.

topStories.headline: District 8 Supervisor Race Thrown into Turmoil as Democrats Postpone Endorsement Vote
topStories.dek: The SF Democratic Party delayed its endorsement in the heated District 8 supervisor race — which covers the Castro, Noe Valley, and Glen Park — after a sexual assault allegation surfaced against leading candidate Manny Yekutiel.
topStories.body:
The race to succeed termed-out Supervisor Rafael Mandelman in District 8 — covering the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, Diamond Heights, Duboce Triangle, and adjacent neighborhoods — has been upended following a report by the SF Standard on June 30 detailing a sexual assault allegation against cafe owner and frontrunner Manny Yekutiel. The local Democratic Party postponed its endorsement vote and has now set August 26 as the new date for that decision.

The allegation was filed with police by Brad Chapin, a former board member of the Harvey Milk LGBTQ Democratic Club, which has endorsed Yekutiel's opponent. Yekutiel has denied the allegations. The party's independent ombudsperson is conducting an ongoing investigation, the results of which may influence the endorsement outcome.

The race features three gay men: Yekutiel, owner of the civic-gathering cafe Manny's on Valencia Street; Gary McCoy, a longtime aide to Congressmember Nancy Pelosi; and Michael Nguyen, a patent attorney who also performs as drag queen Juicy Liu. Yekutiel had jumped out to an early fundraising lead and earned the endorsement of Supervisor Mandelman, but the allegations have cost him several other endorsements.

The November 3, 2026 general election will be the first open-seat race for District 8 since 2018. Supervisor Mandelman, currently president of the Board of Supervisors, is running for state Assembly rather than seeking another term.

moreNews.headline: Grand Lake Kitchen Settles Into Noe Valley Four Months After Opening
moreNews.body: The East Bay comfort-food institution Grand Lake Kitchen, which opened its first San Francisco location at 1199 Church Street in Noe Valley in March 2026, has earned a glowing review from Mission Local, published July 30. Co-owners May Seto Wasem and Dave Wasem took over the refurbished space formerly occupied by Mr. Digby's Bar (and before that, Noe's Cantina). The menu features elevated comfort food including steak frites, caviar pie, and boozy slushies, with most dishes priced under $35. For Seto Wasem, who grew up in San Francisco and lived in Noe Valley after college, the opening represents a homecoming of sorts.

moreNews.headline: Castro's New 'Entertainment Zone' Enables Outdoor Drinking at Night Markets
moreNews.body: The Castro neighborhood now holds official Entertainment Zone status following a unanimous vote by the SF Board of Supervisors, a designation that allows visitors to purchase alcoholic beverages for to-go consumption during street events. The status has been a boost for events like the monthly Castro Night Market, which draws crowds to 18th Street every third Friday. Castro Merchants Association president Nate Bourg said the neighborhood is beginning to feel the energy of pre-pandemic days, and the Entertainment Zone status has added a new dimension to outdoor celebrations in the gayborhood.

moreNews.headline: Cliff's Variety Celebrates 90 Years as Castro Landmark
moreNews.body: Cliff's Variety, the eclectic family-owned hardware and variety store at 479 Castro Street, marked its 90th anniversary this summer. Founded in 1936 as a magazine and used greeting card shop, the store has evolved over the decades to carry an eclectic mix of goods including housewares, tools, toys, costumes, and drag apparel. The June 6 celebration featured live music, a drag show, and a community raffle that raised $19,000 for the Harvey Milk Civil Rights Academy and the Castro Country Club. Co-owner Terry Asten Bennett, whose family has run the store for generations, has guided it through the rise of online retail, the pandemic, and a surge in shoplifting.
